edge_reviews.statement: An exception applies for married names as provided in 8 FAM 403.1-4(C).
edge_reviews.rationale: Remote exception exists but its content and limits are absent; the local exception statement does not resolve them.

edge_reviews.statement: The applicant is permitted to continue using the previous name if the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name.
edge_reviews.rationale: Documentary-permission exception targets the previous-name prohibition and converted scope retains the material-change case.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies if the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 but has not updated her/his ID to reflect the material name change.
edge_reviews.rationale: Older-than-one-year, DS-11 and unchanged-ID scope belongs to the suspension duty.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies when the applicant has had a material name change more than one year prior to applying on form DS-11 without updating ID, and there is insufficient time to request acceptable ID prior to urgent or emergency travel.
edge_reviews.rationale: Emergency qualification retains all inherited limits, but the baseline and link are rejected for unrelated object quotation failure.

edge_reviews.statement: Notation must occur prior to returning the documentation, including stating that it was seen and returned, to the applicant with the information request letter (IRL).
edge_reviews.rationale: Notation-before-return deadline is typed as a prerequisite of the notation duty itself; this fails to express the order of the two actions.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies to applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11.
edge_reviews.rationale: Recent-change DS-11 scope belongs to the no-new-ID exemption.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies to applicants who have had a material name change within one year of applying on a form DS-11, if the ID has not yet been changed.
edge_reviews.rationale: Recent-change DS-11 and unchanged-ID scope belongs to the separate documentation duty.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed.
edge_reviews.rationale: Scope repeats the permitted closed-eye state instead of isolating applicability. It is redundant and does not clearly add a governing condition, though it does not explicitly narrow the allowance to newborns only.

edge_reviews.statement: Applies if the photograph submitted does not meet the specified requirements.
edge_reviews.rationale: Photo noncompliance triggers requesting a replacement.

edge_reviews.statement: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant.
edge_reviews.rationale: Good-likeness prerequisite points only to hairstyle acceptance, leaving the separate recency recommendation intact; qualification wording repeats the permission.

edge_reviews.statement: Exceptions provided in paragraph (b)(2) require employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years to be counted.
edge_reviews.rationale: Exception says pre-break service must count without specifying the USERRA or written-rehire alternatives. P006 alone cites the exception but does not provide its contents; those limits are absent from the child meaning and scope.

edge_reviews.statement: The employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her USERRA-covered service obligation, or a written agreement exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
edge_reviews.rationale: USERRA-or-rehire trigger correctly targets required counting and inherits more-than-seven-year scope, but the family is rejected for its concept quotation.

edge_reviews.statement: This section does not provide any greater entitlement to the employee than would be available under USERRA.
edge_reviews.rationale: The no-greater-entitlement limitation qualifies the USERRA absence credit; it is a supported limiting clause rather than an invented exception.

edge_reviews.statement: An employee is maintained on the payroll for any part of a week, including paid or unpaid leave during which other benefits or compensation are provided by the employer.
edge_reviews.rationale: Payroll during part of a week activates the counting rule, with the stated leave cases preserved.

edge_reviews.statement: An employer chooses to recognize employment prior to a continuous break in service of more than seven years.
edge_reviews.rationale: Choosing to count prior service after a continuous break over seven years activates the uniform-treatment duty.

edge_reviews.statement: The applicant may continue to use a previous name after a material name change if the name change documentation specifically permits the applicant to continue using that name.
edge_reviews.rationale: The exception explicitly targets B004 and preserves documentary permission after a material name change.

edge_reviews.statement: Employment periods preceding a break in service of more than seven years must be counted in determining whether the employee has been employed by the employer for at least 12 months where the employee's break in service is occasioned by the fulfillment of his or her Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act (USERRA), 38 U.S.C. 4301, et seq., covered service obligation, or where a written agreement, including a collective bargaining agreement, exists concerning the employer's intention to rehire the employee after the break in service.
edge_reviews.rationale: B002 is the not-required-to-count baseline. The exception preserves more-than-seven-year timing and both USERRA and written-rehire alternatives with their correct source range.

edge_reviews.statement: The prohibition does not apply to the carriage of firearms and other weapons on or about the individual's person or accessible property if the individual is law enforcement personnel required to carry a firearm or other weapons while in the performance of law enforcement duty at the airport, an individual authorized to carry a weapon in accordance with §§ 1544.219, 1544.221, 1544.223, 1546.211, or subpart B of part 1562 of this chapter, or an individual authorized to carry a weapon in a sterile area under a security program.
edge_reviews.rationale: The exception targets accessible-property prohibition B000 only, covers all three categories, and limits its object to firearms/other weapons rather than explosives/incendiaries or checked-baggage prohibitions.

statement / not_required violates existing kind-modality constraints. The invalid candidate remains in raw/refusal artifacts and is not repaired by relationship enrichment.
MAX_TOKENS with incomplete JSON: 15730 reported thought tokens and 640 candidate tokens. No partial salvage or retry.

findings: Meaning-only uses 43.5 percent fewer reported tokens across all four calls, including the failed all-fields response. On the three documents where both responses are complete, the reduction is 32.6 percent.
All-fields yields 29 accepted baseline statements across three documents; meaning-first yields 38 across four. These counts are not semantic recall scores.

The smaller schema deliberately omits separate concepts, claimants, normalized values, effective dates and actor/action/object records. Its broader survival does not make it feature-equivalent to the all-fields output.

The relationship pass adds only three explicit links, all supported in this review. It returns no photo links and no explicit unloaded-firearm qualification. Conditions still survive in first-pass statement/scope fields and existing ApplicabilityScope/EvidenceBinding records.
The combined path uses 102097 tokens, 80.8 percent more than all-fields and about 3.2 times meaning-only. 43927 of the extra relationship-pass tokens are reported thought tokens.

New-excerpt meaning-first output retains the eligibility conjunction, both seven-year comparators as written, the USERRA/rehire alternatives, all checked-baggage conditions, and the limited scope of ammunition language.

Residual meaning problems include the fused identity fact/possibility and incomplete standalone nonconsecutive-months qualification. The relationship pass cannot repair missing or incorrect baseline statements by design.

First-pass identities, records and original graph nodes are unchanged in composed results. New relationship nodes receive second-pass lineage. All 38 accepted target aliases were returned once; this is processing coverage, not semantic completeness.
next_steps: Consolidate the meaning-first schema and passage-reference mechanics as the next extraction candidate, then verify another small batch before changing defaults.
Address the invalid kind/modality refusal using existing profile semantics, and keep optional component failures from discarding an otherwise faithful baseline. Preserve raw failures and evidence.
Reuse existing applicability and evidence records for conditions already captured. Evaluate targeted relationship requests only when a consumer needs a specific unresolved connection.
Retain the current model, temperature and budgets until a separate controlled budget experiment justifies changing them; this trial does not isolate prompt, field-count and reasoning effects.
limits: Four short excerpts, one live response per stage, known failure-informed guidance, no independent reviewer or repeatability estimate. Complete responses and accepted graphs do not establish legal correctness or semantic completeness. Review judgments are revisable.
